items.title: AI relief fails to lift legacy IT stocks as earnings worries weigh
items.description: The Indian IT sector has seen a rollercoaster of activity, where mid-sized companies have outperformed their larger peers recently. Increased deal bookings are promising, yet slow revenue growth due to client indecision lingers. The emergence of AI technology brings both new possibilities and pricing pressures for classic services. To sustain their margins in this shifting landscape, companies are honing their operational efficiency.

items.title: Stock picks of the week: 6 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 28% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: It is not time yet to abandon the discipline that got you through the bad patch which the market has seen in the last over two years. So, get sound companies on a watchlist and keep a close eye on two key global factors.

items.title: Softbank continues to offload Indian equities, sells Meesho shares worth Rs 1,885 cr. Which other stocks did it sell this year?
items.description: SoftBank Group-backed investment vehicle SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC sold 7.64 crore shares of Bengaluru-based Meesho at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece on Friday, according to block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). This takes the total value of the deal to a little over Rs 1,885 crore.

items.title: S Naren’s art of contra investing: HDFC Bank, Natco Pharma, other 7 top picks down up to 39% from 52-week highs. What this means
items.description: The portfolio of this contra fund is spread across 13 sectors with highest allocation in retailing of around 12.17%. This was followed by 11.79% in automobiles and ancillaries, and 11.21% in the healthcare sector. The fund holds 42.35% in large caps, 17.89% in mid caps, 24.27% in small caps, and 15.5% in others.

items.title: 6 out of 10 top performing largecap stocks in November delivered multibagger returns in long run. Do you own any?
items.description: The Indian stock market has seen a stellar rebound in November, with Sensex soaring over 7,000 points and Nifty rallying more than 9% in just the first half of the month as a sharp surge in FII buying following months of selloff, along with other factors boosted investor sentiment on Dalal Street. One of the key trends noticeable during this bull attack was the outperformance of the largecaps over midcaps and smallcaps. During the same period of time, Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices gained 7-8%. Here are the 10 largecap stocks that recorded the biggest jump in November so far, including six who have delivered multibagger returns in the longer run.

items.title: Tenbaggers on Dalal Street! These 17 stocks delivered over 1,000% returns in 5 years. What Peter Lynch’s rules say to find the next?
items.description: The Indian stock market has seen sharp upswings and downswings over the past five years. Benchmark index Nifty 50 has overall delivered around 39% returns over five years, while Sensex gained 34%. This year the volatility spiked as AI’s seesaw trade followed by Middle East crisis impact rattled market.

items.title: General insurers clock 10.5% premium growth in October
items.description: General insurance companies in India saw a 10.5% increase in gross direct premium income in October. Standalone health insurers also reported significant growth, outperforming general insurers in several areas. HDFC ERGO and SBI General led the performance among private insurers with impressive increases in premium income. Public sector insurers like National Insurance also experienced growth, though some faced declines.

items.title: Softbank further trims India exposure, offloads Meesho shares worth Rs 1,885 cr
items.description: In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

items.title: Can markets extend gains amid rising crude and rate hike fears?
items.description: The Indian stock indices experienced a retreat as increasing crude oil costs negatively impacted market sentiment. Retail inflation hit 6.09% in October, breaching the tolerance threshold set by the Reserve Bank of India. This spike raised alarms about possible future rate adjustments. Sectors like realty, auto, and cement faced considerable selling activity due to these economic dynamics. However, the benchmarks concluded the week with minor gains.

items.title: Dodging bullet loans hurt gold NBFCs after RBI’s revised lending rules trigger repayment stress
items.description: Non-banking financial companies have begun reassessing gold loan structures following increased delinquencies in recent months. Bajaj Finance and Manappuram Finance are shifting towards longer-tenure loans in response to customer difficulties. Many borrowers are struggling to adapt to new repayment schedules that require more frequent payments. Muthoot Finance has also reported a significant rise in overdue loans tied to repayment structure changes.

items.title: ASA International set to exit India by year-end
items.description: ASA International is in the process of exiting its India operations by the end of this year. The Reserve Bank of India approved the voluntary surrender of ASA's NBFC-MFI license for its India subsidiary. Financial difficulties and regulatory complexities have significantly impacted the company's operations in India since the Covid pandemic began. ASA has reported a reduction in its client base to approximately 9,000 after halting loan disbursals.

items.title: Coca-Cola CEO to visit India ahead of HCCH $1-billion listing
items.description: Coca-Cola's CEO, Henrique Braun, is visiting India for three days to discuss the upcoming IPO of Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings. His schedule includes meetings with various stakeholders including bottling partners and bankers. The IPO is expected to reduce Coca-Cola's holding in HCCH from 60% to 45%. Additionally, India is emerging as a pivotal market for Coca-Cola amid increasing competition. The company's valuation is projected at around $10 billion following the IPO.

items.title: Warburg Pincus picks up Rs 1,663 crore stake in unit of Pricol
items.description: Warburg Pincus will acquire a 38% stake in Pricol’s driver information and connected vehicle solutions business for ₹1,663 crore through its affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments. The business, which makes digital dashboards and instrument clusters for automakers such as TVS, Honda, Royal Enfield and Ather Energy, will be demerged into a separate entity called Pricol Autotech.

items.title: India's balance of payments surplus soars to $66.8 billion in H1 FY27 on strong bank deposit inflows
items.description: The current account deficit meanwhile widened to $25.8 billion for the first six months of FY27 from $18 billion on account of unfavourable merchandise flows. The exports grew to 265.3 billion for the six month period against $221.5 billion in the year-ago period while imports growth outpaced it $441.4 billion from $379.6 billion.

items.title: Festive demand drives bank credit growth to 19.5% in October
items.description: The credit growth improved from 18.2% seen a fortnight back while credit expanded at 19.4% pace till September. The outstanding bank credit stood at Rs 231.8 lakh crore at the end of October.
